# Nexis AI — 30-Day AI Governance & Pilot Diagnostic

> Fixed-price, 30-day AI diagnostic for 100–400-bed community hospitals and small health systems in Maryland, DC, Pennsylvania, and Virginia with no full-time CIO.

## The One Buyer Only
The CEO, COO, or Board Chair of a 100–400-bed community hospital or small health system in Maryland, DC, Pennsylvania, or Virginia that has NO full-time CIO (or an interim CIO), runs Epic or MEDITECH, and already has AI tools/pilots running without a single governed list of what is in use, who owns it, and what it costs.

## The Three Problems Solved
1. AI pilots are running in different departments with no single inventory.
2. Nobody can say which pilots are safe to scale, which should be stopped, and who is accountable if one goes wrong.
3. The board is being asked to approve AI spending without a risk-tiered, costed list.

## The One Offer: 30-Day AI Governance & Pilot Diagnostic
- Name: "30-Day AI Governance & Pilot Diagnostic"
- Fixed price: $6,500, one-time (50% on booking, 50% on delivery of findings briefing).
- Fixed timeframe: 30 calendar days from kickoff.
- Capacity cap: Maximum 2 diagnostics per month.
- No retainer required. No implementation included.
- Delivered directly by Shafiq Rahman, MS, MBA, MCS, PMP® (Former Maryland State CIO). No junior staff, no subcontractors.

## Exactly Four Deliverables
1. AI Use Inventory & Risk Tiers — every AI tool/pilot found, tiered High / Medium / Low risk using NIST AI Risk Management Framework concepts, with owner, data used, and vendor named for each.
2. Kill / Scale / Fix List — a decision list for every pilot: stop it, scale it, or fix it first, with the reason in one sentence each.
3. 90-Day Governance Roadmap — who decides, what gets reviewed before purchase or go-live, and the 5 controls to put in place first.
4. Board One-Pager + 60-Minute Findings Briefing — a one-page summary for the board and a live briefing with the CEO/Board Chair.

## How It Works (Four Weeks)
- Week 1: Inventory — Shafiq interviews up to 5 people (CEO/COO, interim CIO/IT lead, CMIO or clinical lead, CISO/security lead, compliance/privacy lead), 45 minutes each, and reviews the AI tool list, vendor contracts, and existing policies the hospital provides.
- Week 2: Risk Tiering — every item tiered; gaps in ownership, data use, and vendor terms flagged.
- Week 3: Draft Findings — Kill/Scale/Fix list and 90-day roadmap drafted; one 30-minute check-in with the sponsor.
- Week 4: Findings Briefing — 60-minute briefing + board one-pager delivered. Engagement ends.

## What the Hospital Must Provide
- List of AI tools in use (or department contacts).
- Vendor contracts & terms.
- Current AI/data policies (if any).
- Access to the 5 key interviewees.
- Total executive time required: ~4 hours over 30 days.

## Who Shafiq Is
Shafiq Rahman, MS, MBA, MCS, PMP®, Former Maryland State CIO. State CIO / Chief Information & Digital Transformation Officer, Maryland Department of Transportation, October 2023–January 2026: led a $250M+ IT enterprise, ~1,500 staff across six agencies; co-authored Maryland's first statewide AI governance policy as a member of the Governor's AI Sub-cabinet; modernized mainframe systems to Microsoft Azure; rationalized ~850 applications to ~620, ~$6M in recurring annual savings. Authored "AI Governance: A Local Government Leader's Guide" (ICMA, March 2024).
